criterion_notes.c1: Examines municipal drinking-water network supply, compulsory household/building pipe connections, tariff affordability, and residential water consumption contracts in Barreiro (Setúbal, Portugal), alongside national municipal and rural water supply coverage.
criterion_notes.c2: Satisfies BOTH the plain wording of Criterion 2 and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading. Under the plain wording, it examines Portuguese national decrees and municipal water governance (Servicios Municipalizados). Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading, it directly analyzes concrete legal and tariff rules governing household service access: (1) compulsory household pipe installation and connection mandates (Decreto-Lei 23:707 of 1934; Decreto 29:216 of 1938), (2) rent-based mandatory minimum consumption tariffs and low-income tariff exemptions (initial mandatory fee for residential buildings with monthly rent above 100 escudos, reformed by Barreiro municipality in 1944 to exempt rents up to 200 escudos/month and reduce tiered minimum volumes across higher rent brackets), and (3) mandatory municipal utility ownership/concession rules (Decreto 33:863 of 1944) and restrictions on private well extraction deeper than 50 meters except for public supply (Decreto-Lei 43:371 of 1960).
criterion_notes.c3: Empirical historical/archival case study drawing on primary municipal utility records (annual Relatórios e Contas of the Serviços Municipalizados de Águas of Barreiro from the 1940s-1960s), municipal planning documents, private industrial archives (Companhia União Fabril / ENEF), parliamentary debates, and LNEC/UNESCO hydrogeological reports.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports concrete outcomes relevant to affordability, connection/contract uptake, service coverage, and resource sustainability: high rates of unpaid household water bills in Barreiro (~25% in 1942, 125% accumulated in 1943, ~75% in 1944) due to household inability to pay under the >100-escudo mandatory tariff; subsequent expansion of new water consumption contracts in lower rent brackets from 1944 after raising the exemption threshold to 200 escudos; national municipal/rural supply coverage rates in 1956; and groundwater overexploitation (779% extraction growth 1961-1978) and salinization.
criterion_notes.c5: Population and units of analysis (municipality of Barreiro and residential buildings/households stratified by monthly rent, plus industrial users and Portuguese localities), rule-type exposures (compulsory connection mandates, rent-tiered minimum tariffs/exemptions, municipalization), outcomes (bill non-payment/arrears, new consumption contracts, consumption volumes, aquifer depletion/salinization), and study design (historical archival case study) are all clearly identifiable. Note that while Tables 1-3 appear as unextracted images in the text dump, the prose reports exact regulatory thresholds, arrears shares, directional contract uptake, and extraction trends; per Criterion 6, extractable effect-size tables are a quantitative-synthesis gate rather than a review-inclusion gate.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Spanish (with an English abstract). Per Inclusion Criterion 10, non-English/Portuguese/Dutch studies are eligible when translation from the full text is feasible and the study is potentially important; Spanish comprehension/translation from the provided full text is directly feasible, and translation method/translator should be logged in extraction_note during data extraction.

evidence_quotes.quote: Por entonces, se estableció la instalación obligatoria de canalización a la red de distribución del agua y del pago del servicio y suministro para todos los bloques o casas con cierto nivel de renta

La metodología empleada para la realización de esta investigación es la revisión sistemática de material de archivo, publicaciones e informes institucionales, actas parlamentarias y legislación. Las fuentes de la investigación son escritas, sobre todo informes anuales de los Serviços Municipalizados de Barreiro, más conocidos como relatórios e contas da gerência.
Es decir, los abastecimientos de agua de las sedes de los ayuntamientos debían ser explotados mediante el régimen de los Serviços Municipalizados (SM) o a través de concesión

Esto se puede inferir del volumen de recibos de impago del suministro del agua que fueron en aumento durante los primeros años. En el año 1942, casi un cuarto de los recibos expedidos no fue pagado, en el año 1943 se acumulaba el 125% y al año siguiente las tres cuartas partes

el ayuntamiento del municipio decidió, ante esta tesitura, aumentar el nivel de renta de pago obligatorio a doscientos escudos o, lo que es lo mismo, declaró la exención total del pago del consumo hasta rentas de doscientos escudos mensuales y la reducción proporcional de las tasas para los siguientes tramos. Así, los bloques de viviendas con rentas de entre doscientos y cuatrocientos escudos abonaban dos metros cúbicos de consumo mínimo de agua. Las rentas entre cuatrocientos y ochocientos escudos, tres metros cúbicos, y, por último, las rentas superiores a ochocientos escudos pagaban cinco metros cúbicos de agua obligatorios. Esta medida posibilitó que el ayuntamiento obtuviese nuevos contratos de consumo en los escalones más reducidos a partir del año 1944

raw_response.exposure: Mandatory household pipe installation and public network connection rules (Decreto-Lei 23:707 of 1934; Decreto 29:216 of 1938), rent-tiered mandatory minimum water consumption fees and low-income exemptions (initial >100 escudos rent threshold and 1944 Barreiro municipal reform exempting rents up to 200 escudos/month with reduced tiered minimums), mandatory municipal utility governance via Serviços Municipalizados or concession (Decreto 33:863 of 1944), and restrictions on private well drilling >50 m (Decreto-Lei 43:371 of 1960)
raw_response.outcome: Household water bill non-payment/arrears (~25% unpaid in 1942, 125% accumulated in 1943, ~75% in 1944 due to affordability constraints), uptake of new municipal water consumption contracts in lower-rent residential brackets from 1944 onward, domestic and industrial water consumption volumes, national locality supply coverage, and aquifer overexploitation/salinization
raw_response.population_and_sample: Municipality of Barreiro (Setúbal, Portugal), specifically residential buildings/households stratified by monthly rent and industrial consumers served by the Serviços Municipalizados de Águas (1930s-1980s), contextualized within mainland Portuguese municipalities and rural localities
raw_response.rationale: Include. This archival socio-legal and environmental-history case study examines the municipal drinking-water network in Barreiro, Portugal, using primary annual reports of the Serviços Municipalizados de Águas, municipal planning records, corporate archives, and legislation. It directly analyzes rule-type legal and tariff mechanisms governing household water access—compulsory domestic pipe connection mandates, rent-based minimum consumption charges and low-income tariff exemptions, and mandatory municipal utility ownership—and documents concrete empirical access and affordability outcomes, including widespread bill arrears under the initial 100-escudo rent threshold and increased consumption contracts in lower-income brackets after the municipality raised the exemption threshold to 200 escudos in 1944. Although written in Spanish, translation from the provided full text is feasible and warranted per Inclusion Criterion 10.
raw_response.study_design: Historical archival case study (qualitative and descriptive-quantitative analysis of primary municipal utility, corporate, parliamentary, and hydrogeological records)
